text: Hold'em, blinds one and two. Buy in with what's in your purse, between ten and sixty-four doubloons.
Table's open. Three locals, one empty seat. Yours if you want it.
Cards don't care who you are, captain. That's what I like about them.
Listen to that thunder. Nobody sane is at sea tonight.
Storm's right on top of us. Stay in the dry a while.
Every timber in the harbour's groaning. Ugly night.
Rain again. Good for the cisterns, bad for the soul.
You're dripping on my floor, by the way.
Night's when the cursed come walking. Keep a lantern lit.
Up with the gulls, I see.
Tonight? A cautious net-mender, a drunk who raises everything, and a quiet woman who never loses. Watch her.
Regulars. Some careful, some reckless, one or two who bluff like they mean it. You'll learn which is which, or you'll learn poorer.
Two cards each, face down. Five on the table: three, then one, then one. Best five of seven wins.
Check, call, raise or fold. Small blind one, big blind two. Leave whenever you like and cash out what's in front of you.
